utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I would like to deal with a few matters which we can deal with in open session. First, the Stanisic motion for the admission of written evidence of Witness DST-035 and related exhibits pursuant to Rule 92 ter which was filed on the 28th of June, the Prosecution has filed an urgent response for that. First request was postponement of cross-examination. We had the weekend anyhow in between. Mr. Groome, what's the position in relation to the postponement?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am prepared to start and finish my cross-examination today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And can we then also -- so that matter is moot. You also asked as an alternative for bifurcation, that is moot then as well, I take it ?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you asked that we would order the Defence to submit timely any 92 ter statements. I would prefer to leave that for a second. I think the message is relatively clear and unless Mr. Jordash would like to say anything about it at this moment. You asked for leave to reply. Now, two out of the three requests are declared moot. Do you insist on the reply for the third one?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, we would like the application to stand, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll then discuss -- but may I take it that the postponement of cross-examination, the bifurcation, that you don't need to answer to that anymore?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There may be -- I can't remember it off the top of my head precisely how each paragraph is formed, but there may have been more general remarks we made. In addressing those arguments we would ask Your Honours to take into account when looking at Defence disclosure generally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but bifurcation is not needed anymore. Postponement is withdrawn by Mr. Groome. So what you would like to do is to make some general submissions on when submissions are considered to be made timely.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will discuss whether -- I will discuss with my colleagues whether your request for leave to reply will be granted, yes or no, and most likely we'll inform you this afternoon. Then as far as documents are concerned in relation to DST-051, Mr. Groome, you wanted to consider whether or not to oppose against D271 up to and including D91. Have you further considered that and could you tell us what your position is?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, perhaps if I could work my way down the list. Your Honour, the first number that I had from the list that I received from the Registrar was 272. I'll inform myself about 271 during the break, if I can start at 272. Your Honour, with respect to D272, I do not understand the translation so I preserve substantive objections until DST-035's -- I'm sorry. DST-035's comments are not helpful in assessing the admissibility of the document. His comments summarised the substantive content of the document and adopts them as his own. So I'm going to ask someone to look at that translation. I had trouble understanding its import. With respect to D273, with respect to the provenance of the document, it is unknown who the author is. It is a document without any name or department. I would appreciate some information with respect to the source of the information contained in the document. Again, DST-035's comments on the chart do not address authorship or authenticity and simply reiterate the contents as if they were well-established facts. With respect to D274, the Prosecution does not object to the provenance of this document. There is no translation of the document. I preserve our right to object to its relevance and substance once I am able to read what is in the document. With respect to D275, the Prosecution has no objection to the admissibility of this document. With respect to D276, this is a partial translation of a newspaper article. The Prosecution objects as to relevance. With respect to D277, this is a curious document. It purports to be official yearly reports of the State Security Service. I note that in the originals on e-court pages 3, 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, there is a particular phenomenon. Typed in the heading of the document is the word "excerpt" which would indicate that someone has taken a decision to only allow us to see the portion of the report which they want us to see. It is also then followed by an excerpt which appears to have been re-typed on a different typewriter by someone from some other document, perhaps the original. The Prosecution would appreciate some additional information with respect to the provenance of the document, who made the decision regarding what portions of the document would be shown to the Chamber, and what criteria was used, and how can we be sure that it was done accurately. If we look at DST-035's comment chart, it appears that he is speaking about another document. I also note that the chart we received from the Court Officer indicates that 1D377 has been assigned the number D277 MFI, while the Defence exhibit indicates that it is D265. The original is 14 pages and while the translation appears to attempt to follow the original in the pagination, I note that it is -- only has nine pages. Finally I note that while DST-035's comments state that 1D377 describes surveillance of Arkan's house, I cannot find his name in that document anywhere and believe the witness must be referring to another document. I believe what has happened here is that the witness has looked at D265 which is 1D00037 and that his comments relate to that document. So the first complete row on page 2 of DST-035's comments appear to need some correction. With respect to D278, DST-035 recognises this material as material he participated in the preparation of, and therefore the Prosecution has no objection to the provenance or admissibility of this document. Your Honours, with respect to D279 to D290, these are documents related to the commission. There are no translations provided yet. We preserve our objection as to the provenance of these documents and we also reserve our objection on other grounds until there is a translation that we're able to read. And finally, D291 is also -- I'm sorry, D291, I note that the document appears to be a redaction and we would ask what is known about that redaction and whether Mr. Jordash has an unredacted version for our review. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I don't wish to comment on much of what Mr. Groome has said, but I do for the record want to, if I may, comment on the issue of redactions and excerpts. My investigator and consultant had an appointment with the National Council last week concerning this issue. Unfortunately, they continue to maintain that they will not disclose full annual reports of the state security. They maintain that excerpts is all that we will receive. And they maintain that the redactions will persist. And I haven't as yet had a full opportunity to speak to Mr. Stanisic, but I know that his view is that we should file a motion forthwith and that is our preliminary intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean a motion for the Chamber to order the -- to be provided with the full unredacted version?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- the lack of co-operation we're receiving from the National Council is getting worse and I think we're left with little choice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If I put everything together, first, when I started saying 271 up to 291, of course 271 itself is the chart, so the first document we start with on the chart is D272. If I listened well, there are two documents against which there's no opposition to be admitted, that would be D275 and D278.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D275 and D278 are admitted into evidence under seal. All the others are MFI'd under seal, Madam Registrar, if I'm -- if I -- if my recollection is serving me well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Then we had documents -- I think it was P1412 and 1D3449. I think P1412 were once on a Prosecution list, although they have not been -- it has not been MFI'd. Any position in relation to these documents? At least I remember for 1D3449, the parties said that they would check during the break - I don't know what break that was - to discuss the matter. For these two documents at this moment, Mr. Jordash, do you still tender them and have your conversations with the Prosecution led to any further result?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In relation to 1D3449, I think my learned friend is going to cross-examine on it. That was where we left our conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And then I'll make a decision at that point whether to apply to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In relation to 1412 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll just check, was that a --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's the 22nd Session of the Supreme Defence Council minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but 1412, was it the 65 ter number or P exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 65 ter number, P or D?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Neither.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: 65 ter, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's 65 ter Prosecution document 1412. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If the Prosecution would consider the position in relation to bar tabling it because I don't think the witness has commented on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would have no objection to it being admitted from the bar table, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then most likely after the break -- we'll have a look at it because documents to be bar tabled, of course, we would like to know what we admit into evidence before we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so we'll check on 65 ter 1412, whether to admit it as a bar table document, and 1D3449, we'll further see whether the Prosecution uses it during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Would it assist Your Honours if we sent a brief summary of what we particularly rely upon and what we were seeking to rely upon in relation to this witness and 1412?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you would do that it certainly would assist and is highly appreciated by the Chamber. Then we have P2984 which is a document which was admitted as an excerpt. I think the parties have now agreed to have the entire document tendered, but not the whole of the document is yet -- is not yet translated. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is correct. So under that file in e-court there are still the four pages. Mr. Laugel has uploaded a full version of the document under 65 ter 6208.1 and this -- now we have received 18 pages of the translation back. Once Mr. Laugel has obtained all the translation, we will inform the Chamber and the Chamber can make the necessary orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I then suggest the following, that the full version of P2984 will replace the excerpt which was admitted and that we change the status of the now entire document to marked for identification under seal, and that once we have received the translation in full that we will then again decide on admission. If that is agreeable to the parties, then we would proceed. Mr. Bakrac, as always, if you intervene we are glad to hear your voice. Then something had to be checked, but this is perhaps not a matter to be discussed in open session, on 2D865 which might oppose admission. If the check has a positive outcome, then we could -- then we could proceed with it. If it needs further discussion, then I'd rather do that in closed session. Had to do something with contempt. Please think about it and we reserve that for a later moment. Then the -- I'll come back later to that. Finally, in relation to 1D2460, I think the problem was that it was not uploaded in e-court. The first question therefore is: Is it now uploaded?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I think is the answer, and we're just checking -- yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Groome, are you already able to tell us whether there's any objection against admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm unable, Your Honour. I'd ask that I do that after the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're invited to do so. Then I think it's time to go into closed session, and for the public gallery to know that we'll remain in closed session for the remainder of the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 5th of July, quarter past 2.00 in Courtroom 2. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 5th day of July, 2011, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
